explanation: SQL JOIN syntax (INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, ON clause) maps directly to pd.merge(how=..., on=...). Your GROUP BY becomes df.groupby(), WHERE becomes boolean indexing.
NULL handling in SQL (IS NULL, COALESCE) transfers to pandas isnull(), fillna(), and dropna() patterns.
PyTorch models are Python classes inheriting nn.Module. The __init__() and forward() pattern is the same OOP you already know.
PyTorch tensors are NumPy arrays with autograd. Reshape, broadcasting, slicing, and elementwise operations work identically.
Same gradient descent optimization, same regularization logic. Only the output activation (sigmoid) and loss (cross-entropy vs MSE) differ.
Random Forest is an ensemble of the Decision Trees you already understand, with bagging. You know 70% of it before reading a single page.
Probability distributions ARE probability theory applied to specific random variables. Your foundation of events, sample spaces, and axioms directly supports this.
p-values are computed from the CDF of distributions you already know. The t-test uses the t-distribution, chi-square uses chi-square distribution — you already have the tools.
Python loop patterns and list indexing directly map to NumPy vectorized operations. Your mental model of iteration transfers.
Backpropagation IS gradient descent, computed via the chain rule through layers. If you understand loss surfaces and gradient steps, you understand 55% of backprop already.
Neural networks are sequences of matrix multiplications followed by activations. A forward pass IS linear algebra.
Both are tree ensemble methods. RF uses parallel bagging; GB uses sequential boosting. Your RF intuition about tree splits and feature importance transfers directly.
Both are supervised classifiers optimizing a decision boundary. Understanding probability outputs and overfitting from Logistic Regression helps with Decision Tree concepts.
PCA is eigendecomposition of the covariance matrix — a direct application of matrix operations you already understand.
You already know the DataFrame API. Data cleaning IS using that API — isnull(), fillna(), drop_duplicates(), astype() are just Pandas operations.
Understanding how linear models work (coefficients, multicollinearity) informs what features to create and how to transform them.
GridSearchCV and RandomSearchCV wrap cross-validation — you already understand the evaluation loop. Hyperparameter tuning just adds a search loop around it.
